prompt: A new, original scene in the same pixel-art style and three-quarter view as the reference. A cramped home workshop that has taken over the room: walls covered in a tangle of pipes, valves, pressure gauges and junction boxes, a short conveyor belt going nowhere, two half-built machines with their panels off, coils of cable across the floor, a workbench buried in parts, tools and spare fittings, and a pegboard crammed with wrenches. It is busy, clever, and slightly absurd: plumbing for its own sake. High on a dusty back shelf, almost hidden, sits the same sketchbook from the reference, closed, with a cobweb across it; beside it a small potted seedling, a little wilted. Daylight comes in through one small grimy window. The whole scene fits inside the frame on a few floorboards, isolated as a vignette on a transparent background with nothing outside it. Pixel art with the polish of a lovingly hand-made indie game: a strict, even grid, no anti-aliasing, consistent one-art-pixel dark outlines, hand-placed dithering, readable silhouettes, a small cohesive palette of warm greys, honey wood, brass and copper, near-black ink (#1C1A17) outlines, and a single burnt-orange accent (#B84A16) on one or two small details. No people, no animals, no text or letters anywhere, no logos, no robots, no glowing brains, no sparkles, no stars.
